1.note: Ezekiel is using **the word of Yahweh was to me** as a common expression of the culture to mean “Yahweh spoke a message to me.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And Yahweh spoke a message to me, saying]

2.note: See how you translated **Son of man** in [2:1](ta:02).

Yahweh is using **set your face to** as a common expression of the culture to mean “turn toward in order to oppose.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [face the mountains of Israel to oppose them]

Yahweh is telling Ezekiel to speak to the **Mountains of Israel** that he knows cannot hear him. He is doing this to communicate to the people listening to him that he feels very strongly about what the people were doing there. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate these words as if he were speaking directly to the people about these places, as in the UST.

3.q: וְ⁠אָ֣מַרְתָּ֔ הָרֵי֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל שִׁמְע֖וּ דְּבַר־אֲדֹנָ֣⁠י יְהוִ֑ה כֹּה־אָמַ֣ר אֲדֹנָ֣⁠י יְ֠הוִה
3.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [And you shall tell the mountains of Israel to hear the word of the Lord Yahweh. Tell them that this is what the Lord Yahweh says]

Ezekiel is to speak to the **Mountains of Israel**, which he knows cannot hear him. He is to do this to communicate to the people listening to him that Yahweh feels very strongly about the judgment he is going to bring on the land. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate these words as if he were speaking directly to the people about the mountains of Israel. Alternate translation: [Listen, you people, to the word that the Lord Yahweh speaks about the mountains of Israel]

Yahweh is referring to all of the land of Israel by naming two major components, the high ground (**the mountains** and **the hills**) and the low ground (**the streambeds** and **the valleys**). If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [to every part of the land of Israel]

Yahweh is using the expression **Behold me** to focus his listeners’ attention on what he is about to say. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [Listen carefully]

Here, **a sword** represents “enemies who will attack with swords.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [I am bringing against you enemies who will attack with swords]
See how you translated the similar expression in 2:4. This also occurs in verse 11.

4.note: The expression **your incense altars will be broken** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must state who will do the action, it is the enemy army that Yahweh will send. Alternate translation: [and the enemy army will break your incense altars]

The implication is that the dead bodies of the people would make the idols and the places of worship ritually unclean, and this would show that the idols were powerless to save the people who worshiped them. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [And I will throw down your slain in front of your idols, making those idols unclean and showing that they are powerless to save you]

Yahweh is using the adjective **slain** as a noun to mean people who have been killed. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [your people who have been killed]

5.note: The pronoun **your** is plural in this verse and refers to the mountains. Thus Ezekiel pictures the bones of **the sons of Israel** as belonging to the mountains of Israel, along with the idols and altars that are there. If, however, you decided in verse 3 to address these words to the people, **your** in this chapter can just as easily refer to the people of Israel. Alternate translation: [the bones of your people]

6.note: Here Yahweh is speaking as if **the cities** were land that would **dry up** and become barren. He means that the cities will be destroyed and left empty. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the cities will be destroyed and left empty]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if **your sacrificial altars** were land that would **dry up** and become barren. He means that the altars will no longer be used. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [your sacrificial altars will be left empty]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if **your sacrificial altars** were people who were guilty and would **suffer punishment**. He means that the altars will be destroyed because of the sinful practices that people did there. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and be destroyed because people used them for sinning]

6.q: וְ⁠נִשְׁבְּר֤וּ וְ⁠נִשְׁבְּתוּ֙ גִּלּ֣וּלֵי⁠כֶ֔ם וְ⁠נִגְדְּעוּ֙ חַמָּ֣נֵי⁠כֶ֔ם וְ⁠נִמְח֖וּ מַעֲשֵׂי⁠כֶֽם
6.note: The expressions **will be broken and ended**, **will be hewn**, and **will be annihilated** are passive verbal forms. If it would be unnatural to use those forms, you could express the ideas in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must state who will do the actions, it is the enemy army that Yahweh will send. Alternate translation: [Then the enemy army will break and bring your idols to an end, and it will cut down your incense altars, and it will annihilate your works]

Here, **your works** represents “the idols and other objects of worship that you made.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the objects of worship that you made]

7.note: Here, **fall** represents “die.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. This also occurs in verses 11 and 12. This also occurs in verse 4. Alternate translation: [And many people will be killed]

The implication is that when these things happen, the people will recognize that Yahweh is the true God, who has the power and authority to do what he has said he will do. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. See the Introduction to Ezekiel for more information. Alternate translation: [and you will know that I, Yahweh, am the true God who has the power to do what I said I would do]

8.note: Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe **survivors** who have escaped from being killed by **a sword**. If your language would not use the possessive form for this idea, you could express it in another way. Alternate translation: [survivors who have escaped from being killed by the sword]

Yahweh is not referring to a specific **sword**. He means the swords of the enemy soldiers in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [survivors who have escaped from being killed by the enemies’ swords]

The expression **you are scattered** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must state who will do the action, it is Yahweh. Alternate translation: [when I scatter you among the lands]

9.q: וְ⁠זָכְר֨וּ פְלִֽיטֵי⁠כֶ֜ם אוֹתִ֗⁠י בַּ⁠גּוֹיִם֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נִשְׁבּוּ
9.note: Even though Yahweh has been addressing the people of Israel directly, here he begins to speak of the survivors in the third person as **they**, and he continues to speak of them this way through verse 10. This is probably because the Israelites he is talking about will be a future generation. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this verse and the next in the second person, as in the UST.

The expression **they were deported** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must state who did the action, it was their enemies. Alternate translation: [their enemies deported them]

9.q: נִשְׁבַּ֜רְתִּי אֶת־לִבָּ֣⁠ם הַ⁠זּוֹנֶ֗ה אֲשֶׁר־סָר֙ מֵֽ⁠עָלַ֔⁠י וְ⁠אֵת֙ עֵֽינֵי⁠הֶ֔ם הַ⁠זֹּנ֕וֹת אַחֲרֵ֖י גִּלּֽוּלֵי⁠הֶ֑ם
9.note: The expression **I was shattered** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. The verse indicates that it was **their heart** and **their eyes** that did this action. Alternate translation: [their prostituting heart, which turned away from me, and their prostituting eyes after their idols shattered me]

Here Yahweh is speaking of himself as if he were an object that had been **shattered**. He means that the unfaithfulness of the people caused him deep grief. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I was deeply grieved]

Here, the **heart** represents where the desires and intentions of the people exist. You may have a comparable expression in your language, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [by their prostitute-like inner desire]

9.q: לִבָּ֣⁠ם הַ⁠זּוֹנֶ֗ה אֲשֶׁר־סָר֙ מֵֽ⁠עָלַ֔⁠י וְ⁠אֵת֙ עֵֽינֵי⁠הֶ֔ם הַ⁠זֹּנ֕וֹת אַחֲרֵ֖י גִּלּֽוּלֵי⁠הֶ֑ם
9.note: Here Yahweh is speaking of the worship of idols as if it were sexual unfaithfulness, that is, **prostituting**. He means that by worshiping idols, the people were unfaithful to him, just as a wife who has sexual relations with other men is unfaithful to her husband. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [by their unfaithful heart, which turned away from me, and by their eyes, that were unfaithful to me by looking to their idols]

Here, **their eyes** represents “their desires,” since people look at what they want. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and by their desires to prostitute themselves]

Yahweh is using **feel loathing in their faces** as a common expression of the culture to mean “loathe themselves.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Then they will loathe themselves because of]
See how you translated this phrase in 5:9.

10.note: See how you translated the similar phrase, “you will know that I am Yahweh,” in verse 7.

Yahweh is emphasizing a positive meaning by using a negative word, **not**, together with a mild expression that is the opposite of the intended meaning, **for nothing**. He means that he spoke with a real purpose and will certainly do what he said. If it would be helpful in your language, you could emphasize the positive meaning in a strong way. Alternate translation: [I spoke with a definite purpose]
If your language does not use a noun for the idea of **disaster**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [these terrible things]

11.q: כֹּֽה־אָמַ֞ר אֲדֹנָ֣⁠י יְהוִ֗ה הַכֵּ֨ה בְ⁠כַפְּ⁠ךָ֜ וּ⁠רְקַ֤ע בְּ⁠רַגְלְ⁠ךָ֙ וֶֽ⁠אֱמָר־אָ֔ח אֶ֛ל כָּל־תּוֹעֲב֥וֹת רָע֖וֹת בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אֲשֶׁ֗ר בַּ⁠חֶ֛רֶב בָּ⁠רָעָ֥ב וּ⁠בַ⁠דֶּ֖בֶר יִפֹּֽלוּ
11.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since the second phrase gives the reason for the result that the first phrase describes. Alternate translation: [Thus says the Lord Yahweh, “Because the house of Israel will fall by the sword, by the famine, and by the plague, strike with your palms and stomp with your foot! And say, ‘Ah!’ toward all the abominations of their evils!]
The word **your** is singular here because Yahweh is now addressing Ezekiel, so use the singular form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

Striking one hand on the other or on a solid object and stomping the foot were symbolic actions by which Ezekiel would show anger and grief about what the people of Israel had done and about the judgment that was coming on them. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of these actions in the text of your translation or in a footnote, or you could use actions that have that meaning in your culture. Alternate translation: [Strike with your palm and stomp with your foot to show how distressed you are]
If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [And cry out in grief]

Yahweh is telling Ezekiel to use a word, **Ah**, that expresses a strong feeling of grief and dismay. There may be an equivalent word or phrase in your language that you can use in your translation to convey this feeling. Alternate translation: [Oh, no] or [How terrible]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe **abominations** that are characterized by **evils**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the evil abominations of the house of Israel]
See how you translated this phrase in [3:1](ta:03).

12.q: הָ⁠רָח֞וֹק בַּ⁠דֶּ֣בֶר יָמ֗וּת וְ⁠הַ⁠קָּרוֹב֙ בַּ⁠חֶ֣רֶב יִפּ֔וֹל וְ⁠הַ⁠נִּשְׁאָר֙ וְ⁠הַ⁠נָּצ֔וּר בָּ⁠רָעָ֖ב יָמ֑וּת
12.note: Here, **The remote one**, **the near one**, the remaining one**, and **the spared one** represent these categories of people in general, not specific individuals. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use expressions that would be more natural in your language, as in the UST.

Yahweh is using the adjectives **remote** and **near** as nouns to mean people who are far away and people who are nearby. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate these adjectives with equivalent phrases. Alternate translation: [The one who is far away—by the plague, he will die; and the one who is nearby]

The implication is that **The remote** refers to people who are far away from Jerusalem and **the near** refers to people who are near Jerusalem when the enemy army attacks it. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [The one who is far from Jerusalem—by the plague, he will die; and the one who is near Jerusalem]

The terms **remaining** and **spared** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [and the one who is still left alive]

The expression **the spared** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the one whom I spare from those things]

Here, **my heat** represents “my intense anger,” which people often associate with a feeling of heat. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [my intense anger]

13.note: The word **you** is plural here because Yahweh is now including the Israelites in general, not just Ezekiel, so use the plural form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.
See how you translated this same phrase, “you will know that I am Yahweh,” in verse 7.

The terms **green tree** and **leafy oak** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [under every leafy shade tree]

Here, **a scent of pleasing** represents “sacrifices and incense that produced a pleasing smell.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [sacrifices and incense that smelled pleasing]

14.note: Here, **my hand** represents the power of Yahweh. To **stretch out** his hand **against them** means to use his power to punish them. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And I will use my power to punish them]
If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **desolation** and **devastation**, you could express the same ideas in another way. Alternate translation: [desolate and devastated]

The terms **desolation** and **devastation** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [an utter ruin]

Yahweh is referring to all of the land of Israel by naming two extremes, **the wilderness** in the south and **Diblah** in the north. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [from the southern border to the northern border]

The word **Diblah** seems to be another spelling of the town “Riblah,” which is located in the far north. Some manuscripts have “Riblah,” here, and some modern translations use that spelling. If a translation of the Bible exists in your region, you may wish to use the reading that it uses.
See how you translated the similar phrase, “you will know that I am Yahweh,” in verse 7.
